user.title: Create a Hydronicus Plant
user.description: Set up a new Plant step by step, or import a plant file.

menu_option_descriptions.guided: Name the Plant and its source, add its pumps, and set up its zones and loops from your Home Assistant areas.
menu_option_descriptions.import_plant: Rebuild a Plant, with the same entity IDs, from a plant file.

plant.title: The Plant and its source
plant.description: A Plant is one heating and cooling system. Its source is the heat pump or boiler that Hydronicus asks for heat or cooling through a request switch; a Plant without one still opens valves and runs switched pumps.

data_description.name: Names the Plant, its device, and its Plant-wide entities.
data_description.source_name: Names the source, such as Heat pump.
data_description.request: Optional. The switch that asks the heat pump or boiler for heat or cooling. Leave it empty when the source runs on its own controls; valves and switched pumps still run on demand.
data_description.mode_select: Optional. The select that switches the source between heating and cooling. The next step asks which of its options means which.

timing.name: Timing
timing.description: How fast the Plant changes mode and how the source is protected against short cycles.

data_description.mode_dwell: After a change between heating and cooling, how long the Plant waits before the new mode starts.
data_description.post_run: How long the source keeps its pumps running after its request ends. Loops stay open for them.
data_description.min_on: The shortest time the source request stays on.
data_description.min_off: The shortest time the source request stays off.

source_mode.title: Source modes
source_mode.description: Choose which options of {select} make the source heat and cool. Hydronicus sets the select to follow the Plant mode.

data_description.heat: The option of {select} that makes the source heat.
data_description.cool: The option of {select} that makes the source cool.

pump.title: Pump
pump.description:
A pump is a circulator that Hydronicus switches, or one that the source runs by itself. Every loop runs on one pump.

Pumps of the Plant: {pumps}.

data_description.name: Names the pump in the forms and the plant file.
data_description.switch: The switch that runs the pump. Leave it empty for a pump that the source runs, such as the heat pump's own circulator; Hydronicus never commands that one.
data_description.overrun: How long a switched pump keeps running after heating demand ends, before its loops close. Cooling stops a pump without overrun.
data_description.min_flow: Whether the pump needs an open loop while it runs, or a hydraulic separator, buffer, or bypass guarantees its flow.
data_description.supply_temperature: Optional. The water temperature this pump supplies. It is the condensation reference that lets its loops cool.
data_description.add_another: Show this form again for the next pump.
data_description.min_flow_loops: For a pump the source runs that needs an open loop: the loops Hydronicus holds open while it may run.
data_description.remove: Remove the pump from the Plant. A pump that a loop still uses cannot be removed.

zoning.title: How is your home zoned?
zoning.description: A zone is the space one thermostat controls. It can cover Home Assistant areas and follow the temperature and humidity sensors that each area names in its area settings. Every answer leads to the zone form.

menu_option_descriptions.zoning_per_area: Each chosen area gets a zone and a thermostat of its own, named after the area.
menu_option_descriptions.zoning_grouped: Add zones one by one, each over the areas you group into it, such as one zone per floor.
menu_option_descriptions.zoning_scratch: Add zones one by one with their own sensors or an existing thermostat, without Home Assistant areas.

zoning_per_area.title: Choose the areas
zoning_per_area.description: Each chosen area gets a zone of its own. The next forms add them one by one, each prefilled with its area.

data_description.areas: Starts with every area that names a temperature sensor in its area settings.

data_description.name: Names the zone thermostat and its entities. Leave it empty to use the name of the one chosen area, or of the floor that every chosen area is on.
data_description.areas: The Home Assistant areas this zone covers. The zone follows the temperature and humidity sensor that each area names in its area settings.
data_description.temperature: Temperature sensors outside the chosen areas, such as a floor probe. A zone with a digital thermostat needs one unless a chosen area names one.
data_description.humidity: Humidity sensors outside the chosen areas. A zone with a loop that cools needs one unless it covers an area.
data_description.aggregation: How the zone combines its temperature readings.
data_description.thermostat: Optional. An existing climate entity that owns the zone's demand; Hydronicus only reads it. Leave it empty for a digital thermostat that Hydronicus provides.

presets.name: Digital thermostat presets
presets.description: Targets of the digital thermostat's presets. Leave a preset empty to leave it out.

zone_loop.title: Add a loop to {zone}
zone_loop.description: A loop is a flow path of the zone: the valves that open together and the pump that moves its water. Leave Valves and Pump empty for a zone that only a plant loop serves.

data_description.name: Names the loop, such as Ceiling or Floor.
data_description.valves: The valves or switches that open together for this loop. A loop without a valve is always open, and its pump is its only control.
data_description.pump: The Plant pump that moves water through this loop.
data_description.modes: Whether the loop heats, cools, or both. Cooling needs a condensation reference: the pump's supply temperature sensor or this loop's surface sensor.
data_description.surface_temperature: Optional. The floor or ceiling surface temperature, the loop's own condensation reference.
data_description.opening_time: How long every valve of the loop takes to open, before its pump may start.

menu_options.zone_loop: Add another loop to this zone

menu_option_descriptions.zone_loop: Such as an underfloor loop next to a ceiling loop.
menu_option_descriptions.zones_done: Go on to the loops no zone owns.

plant_loops.title: Plant loops
plant_loops.description:
A plant loop belongs to no zone. It runs whenever the source is requested, such as a towel dryer, or with a set of zones, such as a loop that several zones share.

Plant loops so far: {loops}.

menu_option_descriptions.plant_loop: Add a loop that runs with the source or with zones.
menu_option_descriptions.loops_done: Finish the loops and review the Plant.

plant_loop.title: Plant loop
plant_loop.description: A plant loop runs with the source, or with the zones you choose.

data_description.name: Names the loop, such as Ceiling or Floor.
data_description.valves: The valves or switches that open together for this loop. A loop without a valve is always open, and its pump is its only control.
data_description.pump: The Plant pump that moves water through this loop.
data_description.modes: Whether the loop heats, cools, or both. Cooling needs a condensation reference: the pump's supply temperature sensor or this loop's surface sensor.
data_description.surface_temperature: Optional. The floor or ceiling surface temperature, the loop's own condensation reference.
data_description.opening_time: How long every valve of the loop takes to open, before its pump may start.
data_description.runs: With the source runs the loop whenever the source is requested. With zones runs it while any of the chosen zones demands.
data_description.with_zones: The zones this loop runs with.
data_description.remove: Remove the loop from the Plant.

min_flow.title: Min-flow loops of {pump}
min_flow.description: The source runs pump {pump} by itself, and it needs an open loop while it runs. Choose the loops Hydronicus holds open whenever no other loop of the pump is ready while the pump may run.

data_description.min_flow_loops: Loops of pump {pump}. A ceiling loop is a good choice.
data_description.guaranteed: Turn this on when a hydraulic separator, buffer, or bypass gives the pump a path whatever the loops do; then no loop is held open.

review.title: Review the Plant

import_plant.title: Import a plant file
import_plant.description: Paste a Hydronicus plant file, format 2. It describes the whole Plant: its source, pumps, plant loops, and zones with their loops. The next step shows the Plant before anything is created.

data_description.plant_file: The YAML of the plant file. Plant settings and the Export plant file action show it for an existing Plant.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure the Plant
reconfigure.description:
{status}

Change the Plant, its source, pumps, or plant loops, or replace the whole Plant from a plant file, then save. Zones are changed in their own entries.

menu_option_descriptions.plant: The name, the source, and the timing.
menu_option_descriptions.pump_pick: Add, change, or remove a pump.
menu_option_descriptions.plant_loop_pick: Add, change, or remove a loop that no zone owns.
menu_option_descriptions.replace: Replace the whole Plant, zones included, from a plant file of this Plant.
menu_option_descriptions.save: See what changes and store it.

pump_pick.title: Pumps
pump_pick.description: Choose a pump to change or remove, or add one.

plant_loop_pick.title: Plant loops
plant_loop_pick.description: Choose a plant loop to change or remove, or add one.

replace.title: Replace from a plant file
replace.description: Paste a plant file of this Plant. Zones are added, changed, and removed by their slugs, and the next step shows what changes before anything is stored. Removed outputs are disarmed, and new outputs wait for confirmation.

data_description.plant_file: The YAML of the plant file, as Plant settings show it.

error.output_bound_elsewhere: {where} binds {entity_id}, an output of Plant {other_plant}. An output belongs to one Plant.

arm.title: Arm outputs
arm.description: Hydronicus commands an output only once you confirm it. Check each entity against the device it controls, then check it here. A loop runs only when every output it needs is armed, and unchecking an output disarms it. Control equipment turns control on or off for the armed outputs.

data_description.outputs: Every output of {plant} with its role.

abort.invalid_plant: The stored Plant is not valid: {error}
abort.plant_file:
The plant file of {plant}. Importing it rebuilds the Plant with the same entity IDs.

```yaml
{plant_file}```

confirm.title: Plant {plant} is not valid
confirm.description:
The stored configuration of Plant {plant} is not a valid Plant, so Hydronicus does not run it and commands nothing: {error}

This happens when a zone that the Plant still needs is removed, such as the zone of a pump's min-flow loop. Select Submit to reconfigure the Plant and fix it, for example by choosing other min-flow loops or replacing the Plant from a corrected plant file.

abort.reconfigure_opened: The reconfigure flow of Plant {plant} is open.
abort.plant_not_found: The Plant no longer exists, or its stored configuration is not valid.

output_not_responding.title: {plant}: {entity_id} does not respond
output_not_responding.description: Plant {plant} asked {role} {entity_id} to change three times, and the change was never observed. Hydronicus keeps retrying every few minutes. Check that the device is powered and reachable and that its state in Home Assistant follows it. The repair clears automatically once the output shows what the Plant asks for.

arm.title: {plant}: outputs awaiting confirmation
arm.description: Plant {plant} has outputs that are not armed: {entity_ids}. Hydronicus never commands an output until you confirm it, so the loops that need these outputs do not run, while the rest of the Plant keeps running. Check each entity against the device it controls, then check it here.

data_description.outputs: The outputs of {plant} that are not armed, with their roles.

abort.nothing_armed: No output was armed, so the repair stays.
abort.plant_not_found: The Plant no longer exists, or its stored configuration is not valid.

confirm.title: {plant}: {entity_id} does not exist
confirm.description: Plant {plant} binds {entity_id} as {path}, but Home Assistant has no such entity. Whatever needs it is blocked: a loop with a missing output does not run, and a zone with a missing required sensor does not call. Restore the entity, or select Submit to change the Plant to bind another one. The repair clears automatically once the entity exists or the Plant no longer binds it.

abort.reconfigure_opened: The reconfigure flow of Plant {plant} is open.
abort.zone_opened: The zone is open for editing.
abort.plant_not_found: The Plant no longer exists, or its stored configuration is not valid.

missing_area_sensor.title: {plant}: area {area} names a missing sensor
missing_area_sensor.description: A zone of Plant {plant} covers area {area}, whose settings name {entity_id}, but Home Assistant has no such entity, so the area adds no reading. Home Assistant does not follow a renamed entity into the area settings. Open the settings of area {area} and choose the sensor again. The repair clears automatically once the area names an existing sensor.

confirm.title: {plant}, zone {zone}: missing area {area}
confirm.description: In Plant {plant}, zone {zone} covers area {area}, which no longer exists in Home Assistant, so the zone gets no reading from it. Select Submit to edit zone {zone} and remove the area. Creating an area named {recreate_name} again also works: Home Assistant makes a new area's ID from its name, and that name gives the ID {area_id} that the zone covers. The repair clears automatically once the zone no longer covers a missing area.

abort.plant_not_found: The Plant no longer exists, or its stored configuration is not valid.

confirm.title: {plant}, zone {zone}: no temperature sensor
confirm.description: In Plant {plant}, zone {zone} covers {areas}, but the area settings name no temperature sensor that Hydronicus can follow, so the zone is blocked and does not heat or cool. Select Submit to edit zone {zone} and add a temperature sensor or another area. Choosing a temperature sensor in the area settings also works. The repair clears automatically once the zone has a temperature sensor.

abort.plant_not_found: The Plant no longer exists, or its stored configuration is not valid.

zone_area_self_feed.title: {plant}, zone {zone}: area {area} names a Hydronicus sensor
zone_area_self_feed.description: In Plant {plant}, zone {zone} covers area {area}, whose settings name {entity_ids}. Hydronicus provides that sensor, and following it would feed the Plant back into itself, so zone {zone} ignores it. Open the settings of area {area} and choose a sensor that measures the room. The repair clears automatically once the area names another sensor.
